title: Drilling Fluid Hydrostatic Pressure (Borehole Stability)

P_mud.description: Hydrostatic pressure of drilling fluid column

γ_mud.description: Unit weight of drilling fluid (typically 10.1–11.5 kN/m³ for bentonite mud)

h.description: Height of mud column above point of interest

applicability: Mud weight must exceed groundwater pressure plus any surcharge to prevent borehole collapse or inflow. In artesian conditions or gas-bearing zones, heavier mud may be required. Too heavy → formation fracture and mud loss.

title: Drilling Production Rate Estimate
equation: T_total = Σ(D_i / R_i) + t_setup + n_samples × t_sample + t_moves

D_i.description: Depth interval in material type i

R_i.description: Advance rate in material type i

n_samples.description: Number of samples to be collected

t_sample.description: Time per sample interval (SPT: 15–20 min, Shelby: 20–30 min)

t_moves.description: Time to move between boring locations

applicability: For cost estimation and scheduling. Production rates vary enormously by method, ground conditions, depth, and operator skill.

title: Annular Velocity for Cuttings Transport

V_annular.description: Uphole velocity of drilling fluid in annulus

applicability: Minimum annular velocity for cuttings transport: ~0.15–0.30 m/s for mud rotary, ~15–25 m/s for air rotary. Insufficient velocity → cuttings settle, pack around drill string, stuck pipe.

title: Lag Time for Cuttings Identification (Mud Rotary)
equation: t_lag = V_annulus / Q = [π/4 × (D_hole² - D_rod²) × L] / Q

t_lag.description: Time for cuttings to travel from bit to surface

V_annulus.description: Volume of annular space from bit to surface

applicability: Essential for accurate logging of mud rotary borings. Driller must account for lag time when matching cuttings to depth. Mark cuttings collection time and correlate with drilling depth at that lag-adjusted time.

title: Air Volume for DTH Hammer Drilling

Q_air.description: Required compressor delivery at surface (free air)

V_min.description: Minimum annular velocity for cuttings removal (~15 m/s)

A_annulus.description: Annular area between hole and drill rod

P_bottom.description: Pressure at hole bottom (P_atm + γ_air × depth + friction losses)

applicability: Compressor must deliver sufficient volume AND pressure. Typical requirements: 10–25 m³/min at 700–2400 kPa (100–350 psi) for geotechnical DTH drilling.
source: Atlas Copco Drilling Solutions, general practice

title: Borehole Deviation Check
equation: Horizontal displacement = Σ(ΔL_i × sin(α_i) × cos(β_i)), where measured at intervals

ΔL_i.description: Measured depth interval between survey stations

α_i.description: Inclination from vertical at station i

applicability: Acceptable deviation varies: ASTM D2113 for rock coring suggests 1–2% of depth for vertical holes. Inclined borings require survey at regular intervals. Excessive deviation affects sample depth accuracy and in-situ test interpretation. Measurement by single-shot or multi-shot survey tools, gyroscopic tools, or inclinometer.
